title: Around 10K protesters expected to join rally vs Trump amid ASEAN Summit 2026
summary: Around 10,000 protesters are expected to join the rally against the visit of United States President Donald Trump to the Philippines for the 49th ASEAN Summit on Tuesday.

blocks.text: Around 10,000 protesters are expected to join the rally against the visit of United States President Donald Trump to the Philippines for the 49th ASEAN Summit on Tuesday.

Protesters earlier gathered along Padre Burgos Avenue in Manila to oppose Trump's attendance at the summit and the Philippines' participation in the Pax Silica initiative, according to a report by GMA News’ Jun Veneracion on Unang Balita.
Clashes broke out between protesters and police near Liwasang Bonifacio, prompting the Manila Police District (MPD) to arrest 11 individuals, including a minor.
Some police officers were injured after allegedly being hit by objects thrown by protesters and being struck during the confrontation, the Philippine National Police (PNP) said.

“The PNP will enforce the law and will not abide any violation of it, especially during this time. Ito po 'yung mga nasugatan natin. Some suffered injuries to the head noong binato at pinagpapalo po sila,” PNP spokesperson Police Brigadier General Allen Rae Co said.

(The PNP will enforce the law and will not abide by any violation of it, especially during this time. These are the ones who were injured. Some suffered injuries to the head when they were stoned and beaten.)
MPD director Police Brigadier General Arnold Santiago reminded the protesters to observe the law and avoid actions that could lead to violations.

“Huwag kayong lalabas ng freedom park. Hindi namin pinagkakait. May mga batas tayong pinasusunod. Huwag tayo lalagpas doon sa sinasaad ng batas. Kapag lumagpas tayo doon, magkakaproblema tayo,” Santiago said.
(Don't leave the freedom park. We are not denying you. We have laws to follow. Let's not go beyond what the law says. If we go beyond that, we will have problems.)

Meanwhile, protest organizers said more participants from different regions were still traveling to Manila to join the demonstration. The protesters did not push through with their original plan to march toward the US Embassy.

“Kailangan pa muna hintayin 'yung iba pang delegasyon galing sa iba't ibang rehiyon na naglalakbay pa ngayon dahil in-interrupt nga. Humaharap tayo sa napakaraming iba't ibang forms of harassment ng PNP,” Kilusang Mayo Uno (KMU) chairperson Jerome Adonis said.
(We still have to wait for the other delegations from different regions who are still traveling because they were interrupted. We are facing so many different forms of harassment by the PNP.)
Protesters maintained that they would proceed with their planned march toward the Philippine International Convention Center (PICC), where the ASEAN Summit is being held.
“Tingin namin mas dadami pa ito at talagang mahihirapan ang pulis na pigilan ang pagprotesta ng mamamayan,” Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (BAYAN) chairperson Teddy Casiño said.
(We think this will increase even more and it will be really difficult for the police to stop the people’s protests.)
BAYAN and other organizations are set to conduct the “Trump Out rally” on Tuesday at 2 p.m., where protesters are expected to march from Liwasang Bonifacio to PICC.—Joviland Rita/AOL, GMA News
